I edit my photos in Photoshop CS5. I have heard a lot of good things about Lightroom. What benefits does Lightroom have over Photoshop? What are some differences?
Should I get Lightroom or stay with Photoshop?

Hey! Thanks for posting.

Lightroom is incredibly useful for photographers and I would say a LARGE majority of professionals use Lightroom for their everyday editing. It's a great way to keep track of all of your files, organize them into collections and subfolders, and of course make corrections to your images. What's also nice is you can work directly from Lightroom into Photoshop. Say there's a unsightly trash can you'd like to remove from one of you photos. First you would edit the photo to your liking in Lightroom, press CTRL+E and the photo automatically opens up in Photoshop where you can clone out the trash can. Once you click save in Photoshop, the TIFF image shows up again in Lightroom in case you need to make additional adjustments.

There are TONS of different features about Lightroom that I could tell you about to try and convince you to switch over, but ultimately you'll just have to try it out for a week or two and get a workflow that you like. What's great is none of the edits you make in Lightroom are permanent. I can go back to photos I edited two years ago, reset them to their original state, and edit them again. You can also make an unlimited number of "virtual copies" so you can try various edits on the same photo without doing any permanent damage.

In short, Lightroom is a great, professional tool to use for making adjustments to a photo. Where as Photoshop is a great tool for photo MANIPULATION where you're physically changing characteristics of the photo (such as the trash can example)

Also, people love to use presets in Lightroom. The VSCO packs are great for getting a lot of the popular looks you see today.

If you have any specific questions feel free to let me know.
In a perfect world, I would use both.
